title: Binary Search and Its Variants
summary: Finding things in sorted data in O(log n) - the halving idea, writing binary search without off-by-one bugs using half-open ranges and invariants, lower and upper bounds, std::lower_bound, upper_bound and equal_range, searching a rotated array, binary search on the answer, and searching over real numbers.

cards.q: A sorted vector has 1,000,000 elements. About how many comparisons does binary search need at most?
cards.a:
20

Each comparison halves the range: 2^20 is just over a million.

cards.q: Why compute mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2?
cards.a:
(lo + hi) can overflow when both are large

hi - lo always fits, so lo + (hi - lo) / 2 stays in range.

cards.q: In {1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 8}, what are the lower and upper bounds of 3?
cards.a:
1 and 4

The first element >= 3 is at index 1; the first element > 3 is the 5 at index 4. The 3s occupy [1, 4).

cards.q: When can you binary search on the answer?
cards.a:
When the check ok(x) is monotonic in x

Monotonic means once ok(x) is true it stays true for every larger x, which is what lets each check throw away half of the candidates.
